summary: Trinity screams as the monitors on the main deck suddenly jump back to life. Tank and Morpheus exchange a look, and the narration identifies the event as a miracle. Trinity then commands someone to get up.

event_hint.one_line: The monitors reboot, signaling Neo's return.

minds.wants: To force the miracle to complete itself; she needs Neo to physically rise, not just have a heartbeat.
minds.feels: A violent oscillation between the terror of the past few seconds (holding a dead man) and the raw, almost aggressive hope of the present. Her scream is not just joy, but the release of the immense pressure of her own faith.
minds.shows: She screams and commands, 'Now get up!' She is loud, imperative, and physically present, anchoring the abstract miracle into a concrete demand for action.

believes_about.belief: He is capable of rising because she has already declared him alive; his body must obey the truth of her love.
believes_about.wrong_because: It is not yet certain that the physical resurrection is complete; he is still struggling to find his footing.

minds.basis: In sc-213, she explicitly states 'You can't be dead, Neo [...].' Her scream in sc-215 is the immediate auditory confirmation of that belief. The command 'Now get up!' bridges the gap between the monitors coming back (sc-215) and Neo actually standing (sc-216).

minds.wants: To confirm that the Oracle's prophecy has held true and that the ship is not left in a state of despair.
minds.feels: A profound relief that borders on disbelief. He has just held the EMP switch, ready to kill the ship if Neo was truly gone (sc-213). Seeing the monitors jump back to life validates his faith in the One, but the 'miracle' aspect suggests he is still processing the impossibility of the event.
minds.shows: He exchanges a look with Tank. He is silent, observing rather than reacting vocally. This shared glance is a non-verbal acknowledgment that the rules of their world have just been broken or reaffirmed in a way that defies logic.

believes_about.belief: Tank shares his sense of awe and recognition of the 'miracle' as a spiritual or prophetic event, not just a technical glitch.
believes_about.wrong_because: Tank is likely focused on the technical reality (the monitors rebooting) while Morpheus is focused on the metaphysical significance.

minds.basis: In sc-213, Morpheus is 'in tears' and holds the EMP switch, showing his willingness to sacrifice everything for Neo. In sc-215, his silent look with Tank contrasts with Trinity's vocal outburst, suggesting he is processing the weight of the 'miracle' label applied to the event.

minds.wants: To process the sudden shift from total loss to total victory and to confirm that the equipment is functioning correctly.
minds.feels: Shock and a dawning, heavy relief. As the technical expert, he is likely the first to realize that the monitors jumping back to life is a 'miracle' because it contradicts the expected failure or flatline.
minds.shows: He looks at Morpheus. This look is a silent communication of 'Did you see that?' and 'What does this mean?'. He is the grounding presence for the two more emotionally driven characters.

believes_about.belief: Morpheus understands the technical magnitude of the event as well as the emotional one.
believes_about.wrong_because: Morpheus is more focused on the prophetic implication (the 'miracle') than the technical reboot.

minds.basis: Tank is the operator of the ship. In sc-213, he is not described as holding the EMP switch (Morpheus is), implying Tank was monitoring the systems. His look in sc-215 is a reaction to the data he was just watching fail and now succeed.

connects_back: sc-213: Trinity's declaration of love and Morpheus's willingness to die with Neo set the emotional stakes that make the 'miracle' in sc-215 possible.

sc-214: Neo's eyes snapping open in the hotel hall is the physical counterpart to the monitors jumping back to life in sc-215; these two scenes occur simultaneously or in immediate succession, linking the physical and the metaphysical.
sets_up: sc-216: Trinity's command 'Now get up!' directly motivates Neo's struggle to stand and his subsequent ability to stop the bullets. It bridges the gap between being alive and being the One.
The 'miracle' label in sc-215 prepares the audience and the characters for the supernatural events (bullet stopping) in sc-216, establishing that the laws of physics are now suspended.
dramatic_function: This scene serves as the pivot point from tragedy to triumph. It translates the internal, intimate act of love (Trinity's kiss) and the external, technical reality (monitors) into a shared, communal experience of awe. It validates the theme that belief (faith) can override reality (death), setting the stage for Neo's awakening to his full power.
